statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) Companies Registry – Company Name Reservation e-Service (https://www.vfsc.vu)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Proposed company names must be submitted in Latin script; names in Bislama, English, or French are accepted; non-Latin or foreign-language names require a statutory transliteration into Latin script and, where relied on for meaning, an English translation certified by a notary.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Vanuatu (unless as part of approved official/agent structure)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection by the VFSC Registrar, the incorporated person or licensed agent may file a written administrative appeal with the Commissioner of Financial Services within 14 business days of the rejection notice; the appeal must set out the proposed name, grounds why the name is not prohibited or misleading, and any supporting evidence (e.g., trade mark registration, consent of the relevant Minister for sensitive tokens). If the appeal is not resolved within 14 business days, the applicant may resubmit the name with an amended distinguishing element or select a new primary name; no statutory right to an administrative tribunal hearing exists at this stage.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is not acceptable as the statutory registered office; the International Company must maintain a physical registered office and a licensed registered agent in Vanuatu at all times. A separate virtual/business address may be used for SaaS/AI operations abroad without altering the registered-office obligation.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low — approximately 5% per annum for a non-regulated, low-risk International Company with no local physical operations; may increase to 15% upon adverse AML intelligence, nominee-shareholder findings, or irregular agent/know-your-customer file.

incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC), Companies Registry Division, Port Vila, Republic of Vanuatu
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form 4 (Application for Incorporation) together with the executed Memorandum and Articles of Association, filed electronically through a VFSC-licensed registered agent
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under the International Companies Act [Cap 222]; shares may be of no par value and issued partly paid; no escrow account or capital deposit requirement is imposed by VFSC for a standard International Company
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the subscriber of the Memorandum of Association is appointed first director of the Company. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the allotment of one ordinary share of no par value and the adoption of the registered office at the address of the registered agent in Port Vila, Vanuatu, are ratified. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the Memorandum and Articles of Association filed with the Vanuatu Financial Services Commission are adopted in their entirety. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the officers named in the register of directors and officers are appointed to their respective offices. step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: VFSC Companies Registry via a VFSC-licensed registered agent (online eServices portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation application confirming the proposed name does not conflict with existing registered entities and contains no restricted words (e.g., bank, trust, insurance, assurance). For AI SaaS operations, a name such as 'VU AI Avatar Video Gen Ltd' is acceptable. Obtain a name availability confirmation letter from the licensed agent before drafting the constitutional documents.
required_dossiers: Certificate of identity of the subscriber/director
Instruction letter from the proposed registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar refuses the name as identical or deceptively similar, file two alternative names within 14 days; no re-lodgement fee applies where the rejection was issued by the Registrar.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: VFSC-licensed registered agent (Port Vila) in the presence of the subscriber or under a notarized power of attorney
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum and Articles of Association in accordance with Schedule 1 of the International Companies Act [Cap 222]. The sole subscriber executes the document; each subscription shall state the number of shares taken. The registered agent countersigns its consent to act as registered agent and keeper of the registered office.
required_dossiers: Subscriber identity document and proof of address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar queries a constitutional clause, the board may pass a written resolution to amend and re-execute the affected schedule; any amendment is to be lodged as a special resolution under s. 33 of the Act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Lodgement of Form 4 and Payment of Filing Fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The registered agent lodges Form 4 (Application for Incorporation) together with the executed Memorandum and Articles of Association, and the declaration of the registered agent. Pay the USD 250 standard filing fee by wire transfer or VFSC-bank deposit; standard turnaround is five working days, expedited (24 hours) is available for an additional USD 250.
required_dossiers: Executed Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where the application is queried, the registered agent shall file a corrective statement or amended Form 4 within 14 days of the Registrar's notice; the original fee is set off against the corrected filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon validation of the application and confirmation of payment, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation bearing the company number and date of incorporation. The company comes into existence as a body corporate on the certificate date. VFSC then opens the company register page and issues the company number for statutory records.
required_dossiers: Company number and register entry confirmation
Share certificates (to be issued by directors)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains a clerical error, request a certified re-issue from the Registrar; VFSC shall correct the instrument at no charge if the error is attributable to the Registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of directors and the VFSC-licensed registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first meeting of the board or pass a unanimous written resolution adopting the pro-forma First Board Resolution. Populate the register of members, register of directors and officers, and register of charges; issue share certificates for the allotment of one ordinary share. Place the statutory registers at the registered office and confirm their custody with the registered agent.
required_dossiers: Register of charges and share certificates
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Internal act; any omission in the minutes or registers is cured by a subsequent board resolution ratifying the first resolution, with corrected minutes countersigned by all directors.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Opening and Payment Processor Onboarding
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed commercial banks in Vanuatu (e.g., ANB Bank Vanuatu, Bred Bank Vanuatu) and international processors (Stripe Payments Europe Ltd and Paddle.com Ltd)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a USD corporate current account with the bank using the certified Certificate of Incorporation and the board resolution authorizing banking onboards. For merchant payments, register with Stripe and Paddle using the corporate legal name, VAT status (zero-rated for Vanuatu-incorporated exporter), and director KYC. Submit the board resolution confirming that the account and processor agreements are within the AI avatar video generation SaaS business scope.
required_dossiers: Director(s) passport and proof of address
Business plan and revenue projection for merchant underwriting
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank or processor declines KYC, resubmit corrected documents within 30 days or apply to a second-tier bank; maintain alternative processor onboarding concurrently to avoid payment interruption.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Department of Industry, Ministry of Trade and Commerce, Republic of Vanuatu — no industrial undertaking or manufacturing license applies to cloud-hosted AI software services; foreign participation is regulated only by the Vanuatu Investment Promotion Act [Cap 252] for physical investment projects, which is not triggered for this digital SaaS entity.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No sectoral operating license is required. The Certificate of Incorporation issued under the International Companies Act [Cap 222], together with the VFSC tax exemption certificate for International Companies, constitutes the complete operating authorization for the AI avatar video generation software business.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Environmental Protection and Conservation (DEPC), Ministry of Climate Change Adaptation, Meteorology and Geo-Hazards, Energy, Environment and National Disaster Management, Port Vila
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — Category 3 (Exempt Activity) under Schedule 2 of the Environmental Impact Assessment Regulations [Cap 283]. The undertaking is an office-administered, cloud-hosted software service with no physical construction, land clearance, or effluent discharge; no EIA registration or full EIA report is mandated.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to core operations. No wastewater discharge, VOC emissions, or hazardous waste streams are generated by AI video synthesis software. If the Port Vila office installs a standby diesel generator exceeding 50 kVA or generates trade waste, registration thresholds under the Waste Management Regulations would apply; all production infrastructure is hosted on third-party cloud providers (e.g., AWS ap-southeast-1) outside Vanuatu's territorial environmental permitting scope.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety clearance from the Vanuatu National Fire Service for the Port Vila registered office; structural load inspection of the leased premises per the Vanuatu Building Code; occupational health and safety clearance from the Department of Labour under the Employment Act [Cap 160] covering workstation ergonomics, VDT screens, electrical safety, and emergency egress routes for a headcount of fewer than 25 employees.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Vanuatu Revenue and Customs Authority (VRCA), Port Vila — central administration of VAT, customs, and business licensing; e-services and tax portal at https://www.vrca.gov.vu; corporate registry and International Company (IC) licensing administered separately by the Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) at https://www.vfsc.vu.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate the International Company under the International Companies Act [Cap. 222] with the VFSC; obtain the Certificate of Incorporation and memorandum/articles; VFSC issues a company registration number but the IC is not automatically granted a Vanuatu tax identification number. Step 2: Because an IC is statutorily exempt from all Vanuatu taxes (including VAT on offshore activities), no TIN/VAT ID is required for purely non-resident business; the Certificate of Incorporation plus a notarised director resolution asserting offshore status suffices as the tax identity instrument. Step 3: If the IC elects to register for VAT (e.g., to claim input credits or to serve in-scope local customers), file Form VAT-01 (Application for Registration) with VRCA along with certified copies of the Certificate of Incorporation, registered agent consent, local physical address, proposed commencement date, and projected annual turnover; VRCA issues a 9-digit VAT registration number within 15 business days. Step 4: For staff or premises, obtain a Business Licence from the relevant Provincial Council or Port Vila Municipal Council, which references the VRCA tax file, but no federal income tax registration is triggered.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone: An International Company is subject to a total statutory tax exemption under section 3 of the International Companies Act [Cap. 222] — no corporate income tax, no capital gains tax, no withholding tax, no stamp duty, no estate or gift tax, and no VAT liability on offshore business; the exemption applies automatically on incorporation, conditional only on (i) no local-source income from Vanuatu residents, (ii) no land ownership, and (iii) no local banking business.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or hybrid mismatch elections exist under Vanuatu law. The only relevant elections are (a) voluntary VAT registration for an otherwise-exempt IC under the Value Added Tax Act No. 4 of 1998 (section 7, voluntary registration conditions); (b) conversion from IC status to a domestic company under Part 12 of the International Companies Act, thereby abandoning the tax-exempt regime and becoming subject to VAT (12.5%) and Business Licence fees; and (c) re-domiciliation into Vanuatu under section 177 of the IC Act, preserving the exemption. Vanuatu has not enacted hybrid mismatch rules or CFC anti-deferral rules; ICs cannot elect treat-through or entity-level taxation because the jurisdiction imposes no income tax at any level.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) — Goods & Services Tax administered under the Value Added Tax Act No. 4 of 1998 (as amended)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Vatu (VT) 5,000,000 (approximately USD 41,000) of annual taxable supplies; mandatory registration for any person carrying on a taxable activity whose total value of taxable supplies in any 12-month period exceeds or is expected to exceed VT 5,000,000; voluntary registration permitted below the threshold; a foreign entity with no physical presence but making supplies to Vanuatu customers is not subject to compulsory VAT registration unless it carries on a 'taxable activity' in Vanuatu (i.e., through a fixed establishment, agent, or local staff).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance API, e-invoicing clearance authority, or digital stamping regime is currently mandated for general businesses or SaaS exporters. VRCA has progressively deployed Electronic Fiscal Devices (EFD) and fiscal invoice requirements for fixed-establishment retailers and hospitality operators under the VAT (Electronic Fiscal Devices) Regulations, which require submission of daily Z-reports to VRCA; however, pure offshore digital-service exporters (AI video generation SaaS) operating from Vanuatu without local onward supplies are outside the EFD mandate. All registered businesses are nonetheless obliged to issue sequential VAT invoices bearing the VAT registration number, retain electronic records for 7 years, and file monthly or quarterly VAT returns via the VRCA online portal as notified in the VAT return filing schedule.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating under section 13(1)(f) and Schedule 2 of the VAT Act applies to (i) exported goods and (ii) services supplied to a person who is not resident in Vanuatu and who is outside Vanuatu at the time of supply, where the services are for use, consumption, or exploitation wholly outside Vanuatu. Digitally delivered services — including AI avatar video generation, SaaS subscriptions, cloud processing, and software licensing — qualify as exported services if the customer is a non-resident, the contract is concluded offshore, payment originates from a non-resident bank or payment processor, and the service is delivered via the internet with no end-user located in Vanuatu; no local VAT is charged and the supply is reported as zero-rated on the VAT return. Input VAT attributable to making zero-rated exports may be recovered in full by a VAT-registered exporter; a wholly offshore IC with zero local purchases typically has no input credits to claim. For an IC exercising its statutory exemption (not VAT-registered), no VAT return is filed and no refund mechanism applies.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Commercial Invoice (itemised, showing 0% VAT, contract reference, and supplier VAT number if registered)
Signed Offshore Service Contract / Master Subscription Agreement evidencing non-resident customer and exclusive offshore use

Inward Remittance Certificate or Payment Processor Settlement Evidence (Stripe/Paddle payout records, SWIFT MT103, or bank statement showing receipt in Vatu or foreign currency from the non-resident counterparty)
Customer Non-Residence Evidence (passport/CRB extract of overseas incorporation, IP address and geolocation logs, delivery domain or cloud region logs outside VU)
Service Delivery and Usage Evidence (access logs, SaaS usage reports, or email confirmation of download/streaming) demonstrating no Vanuatu end-user

Where physical goods or media are exported alongside services: Customs Export Declaration (ASYCUDA World), Bill of Lading or Air Waybill, Packing List, and Certificate of Origin — not required for pure intangible digital services
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: VRCA may conduct an audit within 7 years of the relevant tax period (VAT Act section 61). Where zero-rating is claimed on a service subsequently shown to be consumed in Vanuatu, or where the non-resident evidence is forged or materially deficient, the VAT becomes payable at 12.5% on the full consideration and the input credits are clawed back. Civil penalties: late tax up to 25% of the amount plus interest at 12% per annum (sections 44-45); incorrect returns with no reasonable excuse attract a penalty of 25% of the tax shortfall. Criminal fraud consequences: fines up to VT 1,000,000 (approx. USD 8,300) and imprisonment up to 7 years for knowingly providing false information in a VAT return or refund claim (section 58), plus mandatory disqualification of the IC's registered agent. In practice, export zero-rating for pure digital services is sustained by maintaining a contemporaneous digital evidence pack (contract, IP geolocation logs, payment provenance, and non-resident certification) for at least 7 years; absence of any one element triggers recharacterisation as taxable domestic supply. Vanuatu has no exchange-control legislation, so the 180-day reputational/deadline convention is contractual rather than statutory; failure to repatriate export proceeds within 180 days does not attract fiscal penalties but can undermine the documentary proof of offshore supply and thereby expose zero-rating to clawback.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of Vanuatu (RBV), operating under the Exchange Control Act [Cap. 62], the Exchange Control Regulations, and the Financial Institutions Act; the RBV licenses all commercial banks and authorized foreign-exchange dealers and delegates routine approvals to authorized dealers. The Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) regulates the International Company and its registered agent, while the Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) supervises AML/CFT obligations of banks.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Vanuatu is an IMF member operating under a conventional pegged arrangement: the Vatu (VUV) is pegged to an unpublished trade-weighted basket of Vanuatu's principal trading-partner currencies (the basket replaced the former SDR peg in 2011). Vanuatu maintains current-account convertibility consistent with IMF Article VIII: bona fide trade and service payments are permitted without licensing, subject only to authorized-dealer documentation. The primary legal construct for this treasury is that a Vanuatu International Company (VU_IC) is exchange-control-exempt for all foreign-currency dealings: the International Companies Act [Cap. 222] provides that an IC may hold and deal in any foreign currency without exchange-control approval and, as a licensing condition, must not transact business with Vanuatu residents or hold, use, or deal in Vatu. Consequently the VU_IC's USD capital, SaaS subscription revenue, and distributions are fully convertible and freely remittable; no RBV approval or Vatu conversion arises. Practical hurdles are convertibility frictions, not legal prohibitions: the VUV is a thin, non-deliverable offshore currency with wide bid/ask spreads, so all invoicing, liquidity, and clearing must be pre-funded and executed in USD. Profit and dividend remittance to non-resident shareholders is unrestricted for ICs (no withholding tax, no RBV permit) provided the company maintains statutory records, audited financial statements, and evidence that no Vanuatu-resident source revenue was generated.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the RBV exchange-control framework, export proceeds from goods or services exported from Vanuatu must be repatriated into the Vanuatu banking system through an authorized dealer; the standard dealer condition applied by ANZ and Bred requires receipt within 90 days from the date of the export invoice and no later than six months from shipment, with the export contract, invoice, customs/service documentation, and SWIFT credit advice retained for five years. There is no statutory mandatory conversion ratio to VUV: authorized dealers permit retention of proceeds in the invoice currency, and the mandatory surrender ratio for an International Company is effectively nil (0%) because the VU_IC is prohibited from holding Vatu and is exempt from exchange-control reporting for foreign-currency receipts. For the AIGC SaaS revenue profile, no surrender obligation arises at all: the VU_IC neither operates a Vanuatu export license nor touches the VUV clearing system; subscription software revenue is collected offshore via a merchant-of-record (Paddle) and remitted directly into the IC's USD account. Should any Vatu balances ever appear on the account (e.g., erroneous local refund), the bank will require immediate conversion back to USD via an authorized dealer or onward repatriation, as Vatu holdings by an IC constitute a licensing breach.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_regulatory_note: The RBV has not introduced capital-flow management measures targeting digital services; no Economic Substance filing is required for Vanuatu ICs under current law, but banks impose their own substance gates. The VU_IC must file an annual return with the VFSC, maintain accounting records, and disclose its registered agent and registered office at all times.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.sanctions_and_correspondent_consideratio: Vanuatu has no domestic sanctions list of its own; banks apply UN, EU, OFAC, and UK HMT sanctions screening through their correspondent systems. The VU_IC must ensure no UBO, officer, counterparty, or end customer touches any listed jurisdiction or designated person, and the bank should be provided with an automated sanctions-screening log if the SaaS platform sells to higher-risk regions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.de_risking_mitigation_stack: Due to historical reputational pressure from the citizenship-by-investment program and concentrated correspondent relationships, the VU_IC should maintain a two-bank strategy: a primary treasury bank (Bred) and a secondary operational bank (ANZ or NBV), with a minimum USD 50,000 liquidity buffer per bank and no unannounced velocity spikes. A monthly compliance pack (payout reconciliation, UBO confirmation, substance evidence, and customer-jurisdiction report) should be delivered proactively to the relationship manager.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: USD Non-Resident Current Account (international banking desk) plus segregated USD Escrow/Client-Funds Account for SaaS prepayments
USD Operational Account for International Company (confirm current ANZ Group Pacific retail rationalization status at onboarding; corporate desk remains viable)
USD Operational Account (available only with licensed registered-agent introduction; limited international clearing depth)
VUV/USD Domestic Operating Account (emergency contingency only; poor SWIFT/correspondent coverage for offshore treasury)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: RATING: LOW. Direct onboarding of the VU_IC with mainstream fintech EMIs (Wise, Airwallex, Payoneer, Mercury, Revolut Business, Ebury) is not feasible: none of these platforms supports Vanuatu as a licensed customer jurisdiction; and any EMI collecting or holding funds for a Vanuatu entity would require a Vanuatu banking or international-banking license under the Financial Institutions Act, which no foreign EMI holds. Correspondent de-risking has also reduced the appetite of global EMI banks to clear for Vanuatu-flagged payees. The compliant workaround is a two-tier structure: (i) Paddle acts as Merchant of Record, contracting directly with end customers and remitting net SaaS revenue by SWIFT MT103 to the VU_IC's Bred or ANZ USD account (Paddle does not require a Vanuatu merchant account because the merchant-of-record is the seller); (ii) any EMI pass-through must be limited to an affiliate in a supported jurisdiction (e.g., Singapore or United States) that holds the Stripe account only as a collection conduit, immediately sweeping funds by intercompany wire to the VU_IC under a written payment-flow and IP-licensing deed. Stripe direct merchant registration is NOT available for Vanuatu entities and must never be attempted on the VU_IC.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is permitted by Bred and ANZ provided (i) the VU_IC is introduced by a licensed Vanuatu registered agent (VFSC Category 1 or 2), (ii) all UBOs complete a video-interview KYC with the bank's compliance officer (Microsoft Teams/Zoom with live document screen-share), and (iii) original-certified passport copies, proofs of address dated within six months, and professional banking references from top-100 global banks are lodged. Physical attendance in Port Vila is mandatory at NBV and Ifira. The bank file must contain: Certificate of Incorporation, Certificate of Good Standing, register of directors/shareholders/UBO, board resolution appointing signatories, registered-agent due-diligence certificate, and a clear written treasury mandate. Where the UBO is itself a corporate entity, the full ownership chain to natural persons must be evidenced; nominee arrangements are accepted only with the nominee declaration and the underlying trust/declaration forms disclosed to the bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore, tax-exempt International Company with no local physical office, no staff on the ground, and a pure digital AIGC video-generation revenue model routed through a third-party merchant of record; the combination of low substance and high-distance digital revenue is a classic shell-company and predicate tax-evasion red flag.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: VFSC Certificate of Incorporation and Good Standing; VFSC registered-agent certificate confirming agent and registered office; board resolution and UBO register; three years of reviewed or audited financial statements; AIGC platform revenue report generated by the SaaS administration console; full Paddle merchant-of-record agreement showing the VU_IC as the named payee/beneficial principal; cloud infrastructure agreements (AWS/GPU compute, model-API licenses, domain registrar) evidencing real operations; UBO tax-residence certificate; UBO source-of-funds evidence comprising six months of personal bank statements and tax returns; FATCA/CRS self-certifications.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Reputational and de-risking exposure arising from the Vanuatu citizenship-by-investment legacy and past EU criticism regarding investor immigration, which may cause bank compliance committees to auto-decline any Vanuatu IC with opaque UBOs or unexplained wealth.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written declaration that no Vanuatu passport was obtained or, if obtained, full disclosure with passport number and date; police clearance and tax-residency certificate from the UBO's country of residence; proof of primary business nexus outside Vanuatu (contracts, customer list, operating bank accounts); CRS self-certification and FATCA status form; independent professional reference from an AML-regulated lawyer or accountant; deed of adherence to enhanced transaction monitoring and quarterly compliance reviews.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payment-flow mismatch: customers contract with Paddle (seller of record), the Stripe collecting entity is a foreign affiliate, and funds land in the VU_IC's Bred account; inconsistent invoices or payouts create a layering and commingling concern and may trigger suspicious-transaction reporting.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board-approved intercompany treasury and IP-licensing deed governing the flow from Stripe -> Paddle/affiliate -> VU_IC; monthly payout reconciliation report matching Paddle/Stripe statements to the VU_IC's bank credits; evidence that customer-facing price points and refunds align across platforms; letter of engagement from the Vanuatu registered agent confirming the corporate chain; zero tolerance for cash, crypto, or third-party pass-through funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Abnormal transaction velocity: high-frequency, low-value SaaS subscription payouts arriving from Paddle/Stripe in multiple tranches may trip structuring, noise-detection, and rapid-movement algorithms at the clearing bank.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Pre-negotiated velocity thresholds documented in the account mandate; a dedicated digital-revenue account segregated from capex and payroll accounts; automated monthly reconciliation file (CSV with payout IDs) submitted to the bank's compliance team; sanctions screening log for end users; contractual covenant to notify the bank within 48 hours of any new payment channel or material change in payout jurisdiction.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound funding for the VU_IC (share capital, share premium, shareholder loans, and intercompany advances) must be executed in USD via SWIFT MT103/MT202 from the founder's entity or personal account in a cleared jurisdiction; cash and VUV funding are prohibited. Protocol: (i) remitter narrative must state 'VU_IC share subscription' or 'VU_IC shareholder loan' with the VFSC registration number; (ii) a pre-funding AML pack must be uploaded to the receiving bank three business days before the first wire, comprising source-of-wealth letter, corporate registry extract of the remitting entity, executed board resolution, and executed facility agreement for loans; (iii) the VU_IC must instruct the bank to reject any inbound transaction denominated in VUV; (iv) intercompany loans must be at arm's length with a written term sheet to avoid transfer-pricing or thin-capitalization adjustments in the founder's home jurisdiction; (v) purpose-code discipline: use SWIFT category 'TRFC' or 'MISC' with clear text 'software licensing fees / capital injection / intercompany loan', never crypto, gambling, or regulated-FX references; (vi) verification: the bank's name-screening must match the beneficiary account name to the VFSC registry exactly, otherwise the wire will be rejected on stale-name controls. SaaS collection note: direct Stripe merchant registration is unavailable for Vanuatu; the compliant routing is Paddle as Merchant of Record (Paddle becomes the seller of record, collects card payments globally, and pays out net proceeds by SWIFT MT103 to the VU_IC's USD account, typically T+1/T+2), or a US/Singapore affiliate holding Stripe solely as a collection conduit with daily automatic sweeps by MT103 to the VU_IC under the treasury deed referenced above.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The AIGC SaaS model generates no physical-goods trade, so outbound clearing is service-payment and capital-payment based: (i) compute and model-API costs (AWS/GPU, OpenAI or equivalent) are settled by USD SWIFT MT103 or corporate virtual cards linked to the VU_IC USD account, with supplier agreements and invoices retained for seven years; (ii) subcontractor and licensing disbursements to foreign developers, voice actors, or AI researchers are executed by SWIFT MT103 with payment narrative 'professional fees' and a numbered, signed contractor agreement and invoice recorded in the AP ledger; (iii) dividends and board fees are remitted to shareholders and directors only after a board resolution, solvency statement, and updated statutory filings with the VFSC, with the wire sourced from distributable reserves; (iv) Commercial Letters of Credit are not applicable to intangible SaaS deliverables; however, if the VU_IC transacts through resellers, a standby or commercial LC under ICC UCP600/ISP98 (MT700/MT799 formats) may support dealer credit terms, and the Vanuatu clearing banks will process such instruments only on a fully collateralised USD deposit basis; (v) all outbound payments must be batched to maintain a clean audit trail, with a minimum USD 25,000 clearing buffer to avoid daylight overdraft fees; (vi) fee discipline: instruct beneficiaries with 'OUR' cost code or add USD 30-50 to cover intermediary fees, thereby guaranteeing full settlement and preventing short-paid supplier disputes; (vii) the IC should cap the Paddle payout float at 30 days and require T+1 SWIFT settlement in the merchant agreement.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable USD/VUV spot and outright forwards with an authorized dealer (Bred or ANZ) for incidental Vatu cost exposure; tenors of up to 12 months are standard and require trade substantiation (invoice, contract, or forecast reconciliation).

Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on VUV/USD with international counterparties to hedge forecast SaaS revenue conversion when the VU_IC maintains USD as functional currency and the VUV exposure arises only from a subsidiary or local invoice mismatch.
Cross-currency swaps (USD/VUV and USD/major G10) matched to committed cost bases where cloud infrastructure or contractor payments are denominated in AUD, EUR, or JPY.

FX options are permissible in principle but are not reliably quoted in the thin Vanuatu market; the treasury guidance is to use forward-only dynamic hedging and to reprice customer contracts in USD whenever option protection would otherwise be required.

Natural hedging mandate: the VU_IC must denominate 100% of customer invoices, contractor agreements, intercompany loans, and software licensing fees in USD, thereby eliminating structural VUV exposure; any hedge transaction must be back-to-back with a committed or highly expected exposure and speculation is expressly prohibited in the treasury mandate.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.liquidity_optimization_note: The VU_IC should maintain a two-tier liquidity structure: a settlement tier at Bred/ANZ holding three months of operating expenses in USD (50 basis points or higher money-market sweep), and a remote-sweep tier using a time deposit with the same bank for surplus SaaS revenue pending dividend declaration. Same-day USD clearing is available via the banks' CHIPS/Fedwire correspondents; the VU_IC must provide Paddle with full SWIFT BIC, account number, and correspondent codes to avoid routing delays. Because the VUV basket peg floats against USD, the treasury should rebalance USD balances monthly only when the aggregate conversion need exceeds USD 25,000.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.documentation_pack_for_bank_review: The submission pack to any Vanuatu bank must include: VFSC certificates; registered-agent introduction and AML certificate; board resolutions (account opening, signatories, treasury mandate, hedging authorization); UBO and controllers register; FATCA/CRS forms; audited or management financials; Paddle and Stripe agreements; cloud vendor agreements; sanctions screening log; and the treasury deed for intra-group payment flows. All documents in English; legalization/apostille not required for Vanuatu but notarized copies are standard.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual VFSC Government Registration Renewal Fee (International Company)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC), International Companies Division / Registrar of International Companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due on the anniversary of incorporation each calendar year; no annual return document is prescribed for an International Company, but the annual government fee must be paid through the licensed registered agent on or before the registration anniversary date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment triggers a prescribed penalty surcharge per month of default; if the fee remains unpaid for three months after the anniversary, the Registrar may strike the company off the International Companies Register and dissolve it following Gazette publication and a winding-up notice.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership (UBO) Annual Confirmation and Change Notification
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) Beneficial Ownership Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Deliver an annual confirmatory statement of current beneficial ownership and notify the VFSC of any change in beneficial ownership within 14 days of the event under the Beneficial Ownership Act No. 11 of 2020, as amended.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or to keep UBO records accurate constitutes an offence with cumulative civil penalties and conviction-based fines under the Beneficial Ownership Act; continued default permits the VFSC to impose enforcement sanctions and may be treated as grounds for administrative deregistration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Registered Office and Licensed Registered Agent Renewal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Licensed Vanuatu registered agent maintaining the registered office and custody of the statutory registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Renewal falls due on the annual renewal date of the agent engagement; any change of registered agent or registered office must be notified to the VFSC within the prescribed period by filing the applicable statutory form.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain a licensed resident registered agent and registered office contravenes sections 91 and 92 of the International Companies Act [Cap 222], exposing the company to registry action, loss of compliance standing, and potential strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: None. A standard Vanuatu International Company is exempt from compulsory statutory audit and from public filing of audited financial statements. An audit may only be required where the company's constitutional documents mandate it, members resolve to appoint an auditor, or the VFSC exercises investigative powers for a licensee or regulated activity; the present ISIC 6201 AI avatar SaaS scope carries no statutory license and therefore no audit trigger.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: No statutory accounting standard is imposed on International Companies; the directors may lawfully apply IFRS, Vanuatu local GAAP, or a simplified books-and-records regime. Records must be sufficient to explain every transaction, disclose the financial position with reasonableness, and permit an authorised VFSC officer to verify compliance under section 58 of the International Companies Act [Cap 222].

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the Beneficial Ownership Act No. 11 of 2020, each International Company must hold a compliant beneficial ownership register or, by election, place and maintain the complete beneficial ownership data file with its licensed registered agent. The company must deliver the initial OB return to the VFSC, confirm the data annually, and file particulars of any shareholding transfer or ownership change within 14 days. Where the agent-held route is elected, the annual confirmation is certified by the agent to the VFSC and the company remains fully responsible for accuracy.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Mortgages and Secured Liabilities

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,500 - 2,800 per year for licensed registered agent, registered office, statutory register custody, compliance handling, and annual VFSC fee processing
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,000 - 4,500 per year where a voluntary audit is commissioned under International Standards on Auditing for investor or counterparty assurance

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: None; Vanuatu operates a zero-income-tax regime for all companies, including International Companies (ICs). No corporate income tax, capital gains tax, or branch profits tax is levied.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: VFSC Annual Economic Substance Return — Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) e-Portal. No corporate income tax return exists in Vanuatu.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due within six (6) months after the entity's fiscal year-end or by the anniversary of incorporation, as specified by the VFSC.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company name, registration number, and registered agent details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert the exact VFSC International Company registration number and confirm the appointed licensed registered agent.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Physical address in Vanuatu and nature of operational premises.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide a Vanuatu street address, not a PO Box; for ICs this is normally the registered agent's office unless substantial operations exist.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Relevant activity classification under the Economic Substance Regulations (ESR).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For AI avatar video generation software, classify as IP Business or Digital/Technology Services, and be prepared to evidence core income-generating activities in Vanuatu.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Number of full-time employees, senior management location, and board meeting minutes in Vanuatu.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Indicate physically present employees in Vanuatu; non-resident directors may be permitted but strategic management must demonstrably occur in Vanuatu.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue by source, operating expenditures, and assets maintained in Vanuatu.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report SaaS subscription and licensing revenue separately from passive income; ensure local expenditure is meaningful relative to revenue.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Electronic declaration of accuracy and submission of beneficial ownership details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident ultimate beneficial owners must be disclosed via the filing agent; false declarations carry criminal sanctions in Vanuatu.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late ESR filing may incur a VUV 100,000 initial penalty plus daily surcharges for continued non-compliance, possible loss of good standing, strike-off of the International Company, and disqualification of directors.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Not applicable in practical terms. Vanuatu imposes no dividend withholding tax under domestic law, so no treaty relief or Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) is required to repatriate profits. Vanuatu has concluded only limited TIEAs (e.g., with Australia); where a DTA applies, a VFSC-issued certificate of residence may serve as TRC evidence, but the domestic 0% rate cannot be reduced further.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: 0% domestic withholding on royalty and interest payments. No comprehensive double tax agreements alter this; accordingly, AI software licensing fees and intercompany debt interest may be repatriated free of Vanuatu tax.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No Local File or Master File is mandated because Vanuatu imposes no corporate income tax. However, under the ESR framework, entities engaged in relevant activities must maintain substance documentation (premises, employees, expenditure, and core income-generating activity evidence) irrespective of revenue thresholds.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Economic Substance Regulations apply to International Companies and Foundations. AI avatar video generation and licensing is treated as an IP business or digital service relevant activity. The entity must demonstrate board direction and management in Vanuatu, adequate physical premises, full-time employees in Vanuatu, and significant local operating expenditure proportionate to revenue.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and False ESR Declaration
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Submitting false or misleading economic substance declarations to the VFSC while claiming zero-tax status for an AI avatar SaaS platform with no genuine Vanuatu operations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil penalties up to VUV 100,000 per infraction, daily surcharges for continued default, deregistration or strike-off of the IC, and criminal fines upon conviction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers may be held personally liable for restitution to the VFSC, disqualified from managing companies, restricted from leaving Vanuatu, and subject to imprisonment for fraudulent declarations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company Abuse / Absent Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating as a pure pass-through shell or offshore mailbox entity, with nominees, no Vanuatu premises, no local employees, and no board meetings in Vanuatu, while monetizing foreign AI video licensing revenue.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Revocation of incorporation certificate, compulsory strike-off, and corporate fines up to VUV 50 million under the International Companies Act and Economic Substance Regulations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face personal fines, disqualification orders, and potential criminal prosecution; beneficial owners risk being identified in international exchange-of-information requests and denied treaty benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to maintain and file beneficial ownership information with the VFSC, or using opaque payment flows through Stripe/Paddle to obscure royalty-sharing counterparties and end customers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: AML penalties up to VUV 10 million per violation, asset confiscation, mandatory suspicious transaction reporting, and freezing orders sustained by the Vanuatu Financial Intelligence Unit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers may incur criminal liability for money laundering facilitation, be subjected to travel bans, and face imprisonment of up to ten years for knowingly enabling untraceable cross-border transactions.
